The Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has sworn in Mr Olayemi Sanusi and Mrs Adenike Ademokun as commissioners, charging them to place the interest of the state above personal considerations, political differences and sectional loyalties. Abiodun gave the charge on Monday during the swearing-in ceremony held at the Governor’s Office, Oke-Mosan, Abeokuta, where he urged the new commissioners to demonstrate integrity, humility, fairness and commitment to public service. The governor charged them to remain accessible to the people, listen attentively to their concerns and exercise prudence in the management of public resources, stressing that their appointments must translate into tangible benefits for the people. He also emphasised the importance of continuity in governance, urging the commissioners to preserve institutional knowledge, maintain proper records and ensure that ongoing projects and programmes were completed. Abiodun advised them to familiarise themselves with the priorities of his administration, understand the status of existing projects and bring fresh energy, sound judgment and a strong sense of responsibility to their assignments. The governor further urged the new commissioners to embrace teamwork, respect the professionalism of the public service and collaborate effectively with the ministries, departments and agencies under their supervision. “Your ability to listen, inspire confidence, make informed decisions and translate policies into outcomes will determine the contribution you make to our collective mission. “Bring your experience to bear, remain willing to learn and support your colleagues in the pursuit of common objectives,” he said. Nigerian student wins research innovation award in London Ogun takes wandering girl into custody, begins medical care Ogun Ohanaeze Ndi Igbo endorses Tinubu, Yayi for 2027 elections Abiodun noted that the value of public office should be measured by the problems it helps to solve and the opportunities it creates, adding that the responsibility before members of the State Executive Council was to consolidate existing achievements, address unfinished priorities and leave behind a stronger and more prosperous Ogun State. Describing the period as the final lap of his administration, the governor said the remaining months required urgency, discipline, political maturity and an unwavering commitment to excellence. “We are now in the final lap of this administration. This period demands urgency, discipline, political maturity and a steadfast pursuit of excellence. “Your appointments, therefore, come at a very significant moment. You are joining a government with substantial achievements and important responsibilities still to fulfil. “History will assess our stewardship through the consequences of our decisions and the difference our service has made in the lives of the people. “Let us, therefore, approach the months ahead with a clear sense of purpose and a determination to make every opportunity count,” he said. Speaking on behalf of the newly sworn-in commissioners, Mrs Ademokun expressed appreciation for the confidence reposed in them, assuring the governor that they would not take the appointments for granted. She pledged their commitment to giving their best in support of the administration’s efforts to sustain development and improve the welfare of residents across the state. It will be recalled that Commissioner for Women Affairs and Social Development, Mrs Motunrayo Adeleye and her counterpart in the Ministry of Special Duties, Mrs Funmi Efuwape, contesting for the Ifo/Ewekoro federal constituency and Sagamu federal constituency respectively, had since resigned their appointments to pursue their 2027 political ambition Taiwo Bankole
